chest.name: Barbell Bench Press
chest.description: The foundational upper-body pressing movement for maximum pectoral mass and horizontal pushing strength.
formCues: Lie flat, retract your scapulae and plant your feet firmly into the floor.
Grip bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with wrists stacked straight over forearms.
Unrack, lower the bar under control to mid-chest with elbows tucked at a 45° angle.
Drive the bar explosively upward while keeping your glutes and upper back tight on the bench.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows at 90 degrees (excessive rotator cuff strain).
Bouncing the bar aggressively off the sternum.
Lifting glutes off the bench during the press drive.

chest.name: Incline Barbell Press
chest.description: Angled pressing variation targeting upper pectoral recruitment and shoulder strength.
formCues: Set bench angle between 30° and 45° for optimal upper chest activation.
Lower the bar smoothly toward the upper chest just below the collarbone.
Press directly upward in a slight natural arc over the shoulders.
commonMistakes: Setting bench angle too high (>50°), turning it into a shoulder press.
Excessive lower back arching to compensate for heavy load.

chest.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
chest.description: Allows free range of motion and joint-friendly unilateral pressing to fix muscular imbalances.
formCues: Kick dumbbells to shoulders and lie back with chest high.
Press dumbbells up and inward in a smooth converging arc without clanking weights.
Lower slowly until you feel a deep, comfortable stretch in the upper pec fibers.
commonMistakes: Dropping elbows too low below the shoulders.
Banging the dumbbells together at lockout.

chest.name: Dumbbell Flyes
chest.description: Classic chest isolation movement emphasizing deep stretch and horizontal adduction.
formCues: Maintain a slight, fixed bend in elbows throughout the entire arc of motion.
Open arms wide like hugging a large tree until you feel a chest stretch.
Squeeze pecs hard at top position to contract the inner chest fibers.
commonMistakes: Bending and straightening elbows turning the fly into a press.
Over-stretching below bench level putting shoulder joint in jeopardy.

chest.name: Cable Chest Flyes
chest.description: Delivers uninterrupted continuous tension across the full horizontal range of motion.
formCues: Set pulleys at chest height, step forward into a staggered stance.
Drive hands together in a wide hugging motion, squeezing pecs for 1 second.
Control the eccentric return slowly to maintain constant fiber tension.
commonMistakes: Using body momentum/swinging torso to pull the cables.
Letting shoulders roll forward during the contraction.

chest.name: Smith Machine Incline Press
chest.description: Fixed bar path allows safe, stable upper chest overload without requiring a spotter.
formCues: Position bench so bar aligns directly with upper clavicle.
Unrack with a twist of the wrists and lower with 3-second control.
Press up explosively to full extension without locking out elbows aggressively.
commonMistakes: Setting bench too far forward causing unnatural shoulder extension.
Letting wrists bend backward excessively.

chest.name: Push-ups
chest.description: The gold-standard functional calisthenics movement for chest and core integration.
formCues: Create a rigid plank from head to heels with glutes and abs squeezed tight.
Hands shoulder-width apart, fingers slightly spread.
Lower until chest hovers 1 inch above the floor, then push through palm heels.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips or piking buttocks upward.
Flaring elbows wide causing rotator cuff impingement.

biceps.name: Barbell Bicep Curls
biceps.description: The king of arm mass builders allowing progressive overload and maximum tension.
formCues: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width, elbows pinned strictly by your sides.
Supinate grip and curl bar upward toward shoulders without swinging hips.
Squeeze biceps hard at the peak contraction for 1 second before lowering under control.
commonMistakes: Swinging torso back and forth using hip momentum.
Letting elbows drift far forward removing tension from the biceps.

biceps.name: Hammer Curls
biceps.description: Neutral-grip curl that widens arm thickness and builds crushing grip strength.
formCues: Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other (neutral grip).
Keep wrists rigid and curl dumbbells smoothly toward upper chest.
Lower slowly for a full 2-second negative stretch.
commonMistakes: Alternating dumbbells with sloppy torso twisting.
Flipping wrists into supination mid-curl.

biceps.name: Concentration Curls
biceps.description: Strict seated isolation exercise that eliminates all body sway for high peak activation.
formCues: Sit on a bench, brace back of tricep against inner thigh.
Curl dumbbell upward toward face while keeping elbow anchored firmly.
Focus entirely on peak contraction squeeze at the top.
commonMistakes: Pushing shoulder into knee to leverage weight up.
Cutting range of motion short at the bottom stretch.

biceps.name: Cable Bicep Curls
biceps.description: Constant cable resistance eliminates dead spots at the bottom and top of the curl.
formCues: Attach straight bar or EZ-attachment to low cable pulley.
Step back slightly, keep elbows glued to ribs, and curl with controlled cadence.
Resist the downward pull on the eccentric phase.
commonMistakes: Leaning back to leverage heavy cable stack.
Speeding through reps without pausing at the contraction.

triceps.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
triceps.description: Heavy compound power movement delivering massive overload to triceps.
formCues: Grip bar shoulder-width apart (hands about 12-14 inches apart).
Keep elbows tucked tightly alongside ribcage as you lower the bar to lower chest.
Lock out triceps forcefully at the top of the press.
commonMistakes: Gripping bar too narrow (<6 inches), causing severe wrist strain.
Flaring elbows wide transferring load to shoulders.

triceps.name: Tricep Dips
triceps.description: High-yield bodyweight arm builder that builds rock-solid lockout strength.
formCues: Grip parallel bars, keep torso upright (vertical) to isolate triceps over chest.
Lower until upper arms are parallel to floor (90° elbow bend).
Drive straight down through palms to full arm extension.
commonMistakes: Leaning far forward converting movement into a chest dip.
Dipping too deep below 90° straining the anterior shoulder capsule.

triceps.name: Bench Tricep Dips
triceps.description: Accessible bodyweight movement for high-rep pump and tricep hypertrophy.
formCues: Sit on edge of bench, hands gripping the edge alongside hips.
Slide hips forward off bench and lower until elbows bend to 90 degrees.
Push straight down through palms to full lockout.
commonMistakes: Letting hips drift too far away from the bench straining shoulders.
Shrugging shoulders up toward ears.

triceps.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
triceps.description: Places triceps long head under maximum stretch for full horseshoe arm development.
formCues: Hold dumbbell overhead with both hands cupping the inner weight plate.
Keep upper arms vertical and close to ears.
Lower weight behind head strictly by bending at elbows, then press to lockout.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows outwards away from head.
Arching lower back under heavy loads.

triceps.name: Diamond Push-ups
triceps.description: High-intensity calisthenic variation with close hand triangle placement.
formCues: Form a diamond/triangle with index fingers and thumbs under center of chest.
Maintain tight plank posture throughout movement.
Lower chest to touch hands, then push straight up.
commonMistakes: Letting hips drop or sagging lower back.
Placing hands too far above head level.

shoulders.name: Military Press
shoulders.description: The premier vertical pressing strength test for complete deltoid development.
formCues: Stand with feet shoulder-width, brace glutes and core.
Bar rests on front clavicles with wrists stacked over forearms.
Press bar vertically in a straight line, pulling head back slightly to clear the chin.
Lock out overhead with bar centered directly over mid-foot.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending lower spine under heavy loads.
Using leg drive on a strict military press.

shoulders.name: Lateral Raises
shoulders.description: Crucial movement for building 3D capped shoulder width and the classic V-taper.
formCues: Slight forward torso lean (10-15°), dumbbells in front of thighs.
Lead with elbows, raising arms out to sides until parallel to floor.
Pour water gesture slightly with pinkies higher than thumbs at peak.
commonMistakes: Shrugging traps upward instead of isolating side delts.
Swinging torso and bouncing knees to throw weights up.

shoulders.name: Rear Delt Flyes
shoulders.description: Balances shoulder posture and completes the posterior shoulder development.
formCues: Hinge at hips to nearly 90° torso angle, back flat.
Raise dumbbells outward and back in a sweeping reverse fly arc.
Squeeze rear deltoids firmly without excessive scapular pinch.
commonMistakes: Standing too upright turning it into a lateral raise.
Using heavy weights and jerky shoulder shrugs.

shoulders.name: Arnold Press
shoulders.description: Rotational overhead press invented by Arnold Schwarzenegger for complete deltoid recruitment.
formCues: Start with dumbbells at chest height, palms facing your chest.
As you press upward, rotate palms outward so they face forward at the top.
Reverse rotation smoothly as you lower weights back to starting position.
commonMistakes: Rotating wrists erratically instead of in smooth sync with the press.
Locking out aggressively and losing shoulder tension.

back.name: Deadlifts
back.description: The ultimate total-body pulling power movement for thick spinal erectors and back density.
formCues: Stand with bar over mid-foot, shins 1 inch away.
Hinge and grip bar, wedge hips down, pull chest tall to take slack out of the bar.
Drive floor away through heels, keeping bar dragged tight against shins and thighs.
Stand tall with neutral spine and strong glute lockout.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lumbar spine under load.
Letting the bar drift away forward from body line.

back.name: Lat Pulldowns
back.description: Essential vertical pulling movement for upper back width and winged lats.
formCues: Grip bar wider than shoulders, secure thighs snugly under knee pads.
Depress scapulae down first, then pull bar down to upper clavicle.
Drive elbows straight down and back, squeezing lats for 1 second.
commonMistakes: Leaning back excessively into a horizontal row.
Pulling bar behind the neck (high risk to cervical spine and shoulders).

back.name: Pull-ups
back.description: The ultimate functional vertical pulling test of relative bodyweight strength.
formCues: Overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders, dead hang with engaged shoulders.
Drive elbows down toward hips while pulling chest toward the bar.
Clear chin over bar smoothly, pause, and lower to a full controlled extension.
commonMistakes: Kicking legs (kipping) to generate false momentum.
Not achieving full bottom stretch or full chin-over-bar top.

back.name: Landmine Rows
back.description: Fixed pivot angle allows heavy horizontal rowing with reduced lower-back torque.
formCues: Straddle bar with V-handle positioned under collar, hinge at 45° angle.
Keep flat back, pull V-handle to ribcage squeezing shoulder blades.
Lower smoothly allowing lats to stretch fully.
commonMistakes: Jerking torso upright during pull.
Rounding upper spine.

back.name: Double-Arm Dumbbell Rows
back.description: Builds dense mid-back thickness and fixes left-right strength discrepancies.
formCues: Hinge at hips with 45° flat torso, dumbbells hanging straight down.
Pull dumbbells up toward pockets, leading with elbows.
Squeeze shoulder blades together firmly at the top.
commonMistakes: Using jerky arm curl motion instead of back contraction.
Looking up straining the cervical neck.

back.name: Cable Straight-Arm Pulldowns
back.description: Pure lat isolation movement without bicep involvement for high mind-muscle connection.
formCues: Stand facing high pulley with straight bar or rope, slight forward hip hinge.
Keep arms nearly straight (slight elbow unlock) and sweep bar in an arc down to thighs.
Squeeze lats aggressively at the bottom, then control the return upward.
commonMistakes: Bending elbows and turning exercise into a tricep pushdown.
Swinging torso up and down.

back.name: Seated Cable Rows
back.description: Horizontal pulling foundation for thick mid-back musculature and posture correction.
formCues: Sit tall with knees slightly bent, feet braced on footrests.
Pull handle toward belly button while retracting shoulder blades.
Hold peak squeeze for 1 second before extending arms under control.
commonMistakes: Rocking torso backward and forward excessively.
Rounding shoulders at the stretch.

legs.name: Barbell Squats
legs.description: The undisputed king of all lower-body compound strength and mass builders.
formCues: Bar placed across upper traps, feet shoulder-width with toes angled 15-30° out.
Brace deep intra-abdominal breath, break at hips and knees simultaneously.
Descend until hip crease is below top of knees (parallel or deeper).
Drive straight up through mid-foot, driving knees out in line with toes.
commonMistakes: Knees caving inward (valgus collapse) on the ascent.
Heels lifting off the floor during descent.
Rounding lower back (butt wink) in the bottom hole.

legs.name: Romanian Deadlifts
legs.description: Targeted hip-hinge exercise for hamstring length, thickness, and posterior athletic power.
formCues: Stand upright with bar against thighs, slight unlock in knees.
Push hips straight back like trying to touch a wall behind you.
Lower bar strictly along shins until you feel a deep hamstring stretch, then squeeze glutes to return.
commonMistakes: Bending knees excessively turning it into a squat.
Letting bar drift away from shins placing shear force on lumbar.

legs.name: Bulgarian Split Squats
legs.description: High-intensity unilateral movement for single-leg balance, quad size, and glute hypertrophy.
formCues: Place rear foot laces-down on bench behind you, front foot 2-3 feet ahead.
Lower straight down until front thigh is parallel to floor and rear knee hovers above ground.
Drive through front heel to return to top position.
commonMistakes: Front foot placed too close to bench causing heel lift.
Losing balance and twisting hips out of square.

legs.name: Leg Press
legs.description: Allows heavy leg overload with complete back support and zero spinal loading.
formCues: Place feet shoulder-width on platform, keep lower back and hips firmly against pad.
Release safety levers and lower platform smoothly until knees reach 90°.
Press platform back up through heels without locking knees forcefully at top.
commonMistakes: Allowing pelvis/tailbone to curl off the seat at the bottom.
Snapping knees into hyperextension at the lockout.

legs.name: Walking Lunges
legs.description: Dynamic functional leg movement building hip stability and unilateral leg power.
formCues: Take a long step forward, lowering rear knee until it gently kisses the floor.
Keep front shin near vertical and torso upright.
Drive through front heel directly into the next step.
commonMistakes: Short stepping causing front knee to overshoot toes excessively.
Banging rear knee hard into the ground.

glutes.name: Barbell Hip Thrusts
glutes.description: The #1 scientifically proven exercise for direct horizontal glute recruitment and power.
formCues: Sit with upper back against bench pad, barbell with pad resting across hips.
Feet flat, shoulder-width apart, shins vertical at top lockout.
Drive through heels extending hips toward ceiling until thighs and torso form a straight line.
Hold top glute squeeze for a full 2 seconds with ribs kept down.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back and looking up instead of keeping chin tucked and ribs down.
Placing feet too far forward (hamstring dominance) or too close (quad dominance).

abs.name: Planks
abs.description: Isometric foundation exercise for core stiffness, spine health, and posture support.
formCues: Rest on forearms with elbows directly under shoulders.
Tuck pelvis under (posterior pelvic tilt) and squeeze glutes hard.
Pull elbows toward toes isometrically to maximize abdominal brace.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips down causing lower back extension.
Holding breath instead of diaphragmatic controlled breathing.

forearms.name: Barbell Wrist Curls
forearms.description: Builds thick, muscular forearms and increases raw grip stability on deadlifts and pull-ups.
formCues: Rest forearms on bench with wrists hanging over edge.
Curl bar upward with wrists, squeeze at top, and lower down letting bar roll into fingers.
Control the eccentric phase smoothly without jerky motions.
commonMistakes: Using excessively heavy weight straining wrist tendons.
Lifting forearms off the bench support.
